label.en: Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices

translationRepairs: (Old History of the Five Dynasties, Biography of Cui Zuan: Gaozu ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to restore the civil and military dances and to fix in detail the rites of the winter court assembly and the music sections.

(Ouyang's History [New History of the Five Dynasties], Biography of Cui Zhuo: Gaozu ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to restore the civil and military dances and to fix in detail the rites of the winter court assembly and the music sections.
歐陽史 is Ouyang's New History, not the Old History, and 崔棁 is Cui Zhuo (棁 = zhuō). The proposal rightly rejects Old History and Zuan but wrongly substitutes Zhi.

(Old History of the Five Dynasties, Biography of Cui Zuan: Gaozu ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to restore the civil and military dances and to fix in detail the rites of the winter court assembly and the music sections.

(Ouyang's History, Biography of Cui Zhuo: Gaozu ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to restore the civil and military dances and to fix in detail the rites of the winter court assembly and the music sections.
Literal citation must read 歐陽史·崔棁傳 as Ouyang's History, Biography of Cui Zhuo; Zhi repeats the wrong reading of 棁.

Since the chaos at the end of Tang, ritual and music institutions had long been lost. Zuan, together with Vice Censor-in-Chief Dou Zhengu, Vice Minister of Justice Lü Qi, Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Yun, and others, drafted regulations for them.

Since the chaos at the end of Tang, ritual and music institutions had long been lost. Zhuo, together with Vice Censor-in-Chief Dou Zhengu, Vice Minister of Justice Lü Qi, Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Yun, and others, drafted regulations for them.
Subject 棁 is Zhuo, not Zuan; the proposed Zhi is still a wrong romanization of the same character.

Since the chaos at the end of Tang, ritual and music institutions had long been lost; Zuan together with Vice Censor-in-Chief Dou Zhengu, Vice Minister of Justice Lü Qi, Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Yun, and others drafted regulations for them.

Since the chaos at the end of Tang, ritual and music institutions had long been lost; Zhuo together with Vice Censor-in-Chief Dou Zhengu, Vice Minister of Justice Lü Qi, Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Yun, and others drafted regulations for them.
Literal subject 棁 must be Zhuo; replacing Zuan with Zhi does not restore the correct name.
When the rites were complete, Gaozu was greatly pleased and bestowed gold and silk on Zuan. All the ministers and onlookers praised and marveled at it.
When the rites were complete, Gaozu was greatly pleased and bestowed gold and silk on Zhuo. All the ministers and onlookers praised and marveled at it.
Gift recipient 賜棁 is Zhuo; Zhi is not the reading of 棁.
When the rites were complete, Gaozu was greatly pleased and bestowed gold and silk on Zuan; all the ministers and onlookers praised and marveled at it.
When the rites were complete, Gaozu was greatly pleased and bestowed gold and silk on Zhuo; all the ministers and onlookers praised and marveled at it.
Literal 賜棁 likewise requires Zhuo, not the proposed Zhi.
